newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Southeast power steady to higher on cold.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Southeast power steady to higher on cold.

text.p: Spot bulk electricity prices in the U.S. Southeast were steady to higher Friday, led by stronger natural gas prices and forecast cold weather.
Temperatures in the Southeast are expected to be about 10-20 degrees below-normal Saturday through Monday, the National Weather Service reported.

Firm, peak power prices in the northern part of the Tennessee Valley Authority (TVA) territory for Monday were in the $24.00-25.50 per megawatt hour (MWh) area, as compared with Thursday's range of $24.00-26.00.
Firm, off-peak electricity prices in northern TVA for Monday were still assessed at $14.00-15.00, traders said.
Firm, peak electricity prices in 16 hour blocks at the Georgia/Florida border for Monday delivery were up about $1 to the $25.50-26.50 range.
Firm, off-peak power for Monday at the Ga./Fla. border was still notionally at $13.00-14.00.
In Florida, where below-normal temperatures are expected to last through at the middle of next week, firm, peak prices were talked in the $28.00-30.00 range.
For Staurday through Monday delivery, prices in Florida were in the low-$30s, market sources said.
Also in response to bitterly cold temperatures in the central U.S., natural gas prices for weekend delivery on the Gulf Coast pipes were up almost 30 cents today to the $3.85-3.90 per mmBtu range.
